items.defEn: give up completely; desert or leave behind
items.usage: 可指放棄計畫、權利或人；GRE 閱讀常考「拋棄原則／主張」。
items.exampleEn: She would not abandon the experiment after one failed trial.
items.exampleZh: 她不會因為一次失敗就放棄實驗。

items.defEn: become less intense; reduce in force or amount
items.usage: 常搭配 storm、pain、anger、inflation；GRE 多考「強度下降」而非「完全停止」。
items.exampleEn: Public outrage began to abate once the committee released its findings.
items.exampleZh: 委員會公布調查結果後，民憤開始消退。

items.defEn: formally give up a throne, office, or duty
items.usage: 本義為君主退位，引申為推卸責任；常見搭配 abdicate responsibility。
items.exampleEn: The director refused to abdicate responsibility for the failed merger.
items.exampleZh: 董事拒絕推卸對併購失敗的責任。

items.defEn: deviating from the expected or normal course
items.usage: GRE 科學／社會段落常用以標記偏離常態的行為或數據。
items.exampleEn: The aberrant results prompted the lab to recalibrate its instruments.
items.exampleZh: 異常結果促使實驗室重新校正儀器。

items.defEn: a state of temporary suspension or inactivity
items.usage: 幾乎總與 in abeyance 連用，表示計畫或權利暫時停擺。
items.exampleEn: The funding request was held in abeyance until the audit was complete.
items.exampleZh: 資助申請被擱置，直到審計完成。

items.defEn: regard with intense dislike or moral disgust
items.usage: 語氣強於 dislike；常接 cruelty、violence、hypocrisy 等道德對象。
items.exampleEn: She abhorred any research protocol that put patients at unnecessary risk.
items.exampleZh: 她憎惡任何讓病人承受不必要風險的研究程序。

items.defEn: utterly hopeless, degraded, or contemptible
items.usage: 常修飾 poverty、failure、apology；強調程度之深，而非單純「可憐」。
items.exampleEn: The refugees lived in abject poverty after the harvest collapsed.
items.exampleZh: 收成崩潰後，難民生活在極度貧困之中。

items.defEn: solemnly reject or recant a belief, claim, or allegiance
items.usage: 比 abandon 更正式，帶「宣誓斷絕」色彩；常接 heresy、violence、loyalty。
items.exampleEn: The dissident was forced to abjure his earlier political writings.
items.exampleZh: 那位異議者被迫公開放棄先前的政論文稿。

items.defEn: harsh in manner; causing irritation by rubbing
items.defZh: 粗糙的；刺耳的；使人不悅的
items.usage: GRE 多考人際語氣「刻薄、磨人」，物理「研磨」義較少單獨成題。
items.exampleEn: His abrasive comments alienated colleagues who might otherwise have supported him.
items.exampleZh: 他刻薄的評論疏遠了原本可能支持他的同事。

items.defEn: shorten a text while keeping its essential meaning
items.usage: 多用於書籍、演講、權利；GRE 亦見 abridged rights（遭削減的權利）。
items.exampleEn: The editor abridged the memoir to fit the magazine’s page limit.
items.exampleZh: 編輯刪節了這本回憶錄，以符合雜誌篇幅限制。

items.defEn: leave secretly and hurriedly, especially to avoid capture or duty
items.usage: 常接 with（帶走錢財）或 from（逃離責任）；帶貶義。
items.exampleEn: The treasurer absconded with the grant money before the audit began.
items.exampleZh: 出納在審計開始前捲款潛逃。

items.defEn: declare free from blame, guilt, or obligation
items.usage: 常見結構 absolve someone of/from；法律與宗教語境皆常見。
items.exampleEn: The inquiry did not absolve the contractor of negligence.
items.exampleZh: 調查並未免除承包商的疏失責任。

items.defEn: moderate, especially in eating and drinking
items.usage: 不限於酒食，也可形容對享樂、開支的克制；常與 ascetic 對照，程度較輕。
items.exampleEn: An abstemious diet helped the athletes recover between competitions.
items.exampleZh: 有節制的飲食幫助選手在賽事之間恢復。

items.defEn: difficult to understand because of complexity or obscurity
items.usage: 多修飾理論、論證、術語；強調「費解」，未必等於「高明」。
items.exampleEn: The philosopher’s abstruse footnotes discouraged all but specialist readers.
items.exampleZh: 那位哲學家深奧的註腳讓非專業讀者望而卻步。

items.defEn: an expression of high praise or honor
items.usage: 可數；常與 receive、win、heap 搭配，指公開肯定而非私下誇獎。
items.exampleEn: The biologist received numerous accolades for mapping the coral genome.
items.exampleZh: 這位生物學家因繪製珊瑚基因組而獲得諸多讚譽。

items.defEn: sharp and biting in tone, taste, or temper
items.usage: GRE 多考言辭風格；與 sarcastic 近，但更強調「刺人」而非「反諷」。
items.exampleEn: Her acerbic review left the novelist unwilling to grant further interviews.
items.exampleZh: 她尖酸的書評讓小說家不願再接受訪問。

items.defEn: the highest point of achievement or development
items.usage: 常作 the acme of；比 peak 更書面，多用於成就、風格或文明高度。
items.exampleEn: Many critics regard the quartet as the acme of his late style.
items.exampleZh: 許多評論家視這首四重奏為其晚期風格的巔峰。

items.defEn: accept something reluctantly but without protest
items.usage: 常接 in 或 to；重點是「不反對」而非真心贊成，GRE 常考此細微差異。
items.exampleEn: The board acquiesced in the merger after investors threatened to withdraw.
items.exampleZh: 在投資人威脅撤資後，董事會默許了這項併購。

items.defEn: unpleasantly sharp to the taste or smell; bitterly cutting
items.usage: 本義指氣味／味道刺人，引申為言辭刻薄；科學段落常見煙霧、化學氣味。
items.exampleEn: An acrid haze hung over the valley after the factory fire.
items.exampleZh: 工廠火災後，刺鼻的煙霧籠罩著山谷。

items.defEn: marked by bitterness and sharp hostility, especially in dispute
items.usage: 幾乎總修飾 dispute、debate、divorce、exchange，強調爭執氣氛。
items.exampleEn: The contract talks grew acrimonious when neither side would yield on patents.
items.exampleZh: 雙方在專利上互不相讓，合約談判變得尖酸敵對。

items.defEn: skillful and resourceful, especially in handling situations
items.usage: 可指手藝或手腕；GRE 更常考社交／政治上的「手法高明」。
items.exampleEn: The diplomat was adroit at turning hostile questions into policy talking points.
items.exampleZh: 那位外交官善於把敵意提問轉成政策論點。

items.defEn: excessive or slavish praise
items.usage: 帶貶義，暗示吹捧過頭；常與 celebrity、leader、public 連用。
items.exampleEn: The scientist distrusted the adulation that followed her popular book.
items.exampleZh: 那位科學家對暢銷書帶來的過度頌揚心存懷疑。

items.defEn: make impure or weaker by adding an inferior substance
items.usage: 食品、藥物、數據皆可「掺假」；GRE 常考品質被稀釋或污染。
items.exampleEn: Inspectors fined the mill for adulterating flour with cheaper fillers.
items.exampleZh: 稽查人員因麵粉摻入廉價填充物而對工廠開罰。

items.defEn: happening by chance rather than by inherent design
items.defZh: 偶然的；外加的；非本質的
items.usage: 強調「非固有、碰巧發生」；生物文本亦可指不定根等「額外長出」的構造。
items.exampleEn: Their success was partly adventitious, the result of a rival’s sudden collapse.
items.exampleZh: 他們的成功有一部分出於偶然，來自對手突然垮台。

items.defEn: concerned with beauty or artistic taste
items.usage: GRE 最常考形容詞；亦可作名詞 aesthetics（美學）。勿與 ascetic 混淆。
items.exampleEn: The committee rejected the plan on aesthetic rather than structural grounds.
items.exampleZh: 委員會基於審美而非結構理由否決了該方案。

items.defEn: easy to talk to; warmly courteous
items.defZh: 和藹可親的；易於交談的
items.usage: 強調待人友善、好接近；常形容領袖、東道主、面試官的風度。
items.exampleEn: An affable chairperson kept the tense hearing from collapsing into insults.
items.exampleZh: 和藹的主席讓緊張的聽證會沒有淪為互相辱罵。

items.defEn: a natural liking, kinship, or close resemblance
items.defZh: 親近感；親和力；密切關係
items.usage: 可指情感偏好（affinity for）或結構相似（affinity between）；化學義「親和力」偶爾出現。
items.exampleEn: She felt an immediate affinity for archival work after her first internship.
items.exampleZh: 第一次實習後，她立刻對檔案工作產生親近感。

items.defEn: having abundant wealth or resources
items.usage: 修飾人、社區、國家；語氣比 rich 更正式。亦可作名詞 the affluent。
items.exampleEn: Affluent suburbs funded the museum’s expansion through private donations.
items.exampleZh: 富裕郊區透過私人捐款資助博物館擴建。

items.defEn: increase in power, status, or wealth, often excessively
items.defZh: 擴大（權勢、聲望）；自我吹噓
items.usage: 常見 self-aggrandizing；GRE 常暗示不正當或過度的自我抬升。
items.exampleEn: The memoir was accused of aggrandizing minor episodes into historic turning points.
items.exampleZh: 這本回憶錄被指控把小事誇大成歷史轉捩點。

items.defEn: a whole formed by combining separate elements; a total
items.usage: GRE 亦常考動詞「聚集」與形容詞「合計的」；in the aggregate 表示整體來看。
items.exampleEn: In the aggregate, the small grants amounted to a substantial research budget.
items.exampleZh: 整體來看，這些小額補助已構成可觀的研究經費。

items.defEn: cheerful readiness and prompt willingness
items.usage: with alacrity 為固定搭配；強調又快又願意，不只是速度。
items.exampleEn: The intern accepted the extra assignment with surprising alacrity.
items.exampleZh: 實習生出人意料地欣然接下額外任務。

items.defEn: make suffering, a problem, or a burden less severe
items.usage: 對象多為 pain、poverty、pressure；是「減輕」而非「根除」。
items.exampleEn: Targeted subsidies were designed to alleviate shortages without distorting prices.
items.exampleZh: 定向補貼旨在減輕短缺，同時避免扭曲價格。

items.defEn: mix metals; weaken or debase by mixing with something inferior
items.usage: GRE 常考引申義「因混入他物而減損純粹性」；名詞「合金」較直白，較少單獨設陷阱。
items.exampleEn: Doubt alloyed her pride in the award, since the committee had been stacked with allies.
items.exampleZh: 懷疑削弱了她對獎項的自豪，因為委員會裡安插了盟友。

items.defEn: refer to something indirectly
items.usage: 必須接 to；勿與 elude（逃避）混淆。比 mention 更含蓄。
items.exampleEn: The preface alludes to earlier scandals without naming the officials involved.
items.exampleZh: 序言暗指先前醜聞，卻不點名涉案官員。

items.defEn: unselfish concern for the welfare of others
items.usage: 生物與倫理學段落皆常見；GRE 常對照 self-interest、egoism。
items.exampleEn: Critics asked whether corporate altruism was genuine or a branding strategy.
items.exampleZh: 批評者質疑企業利他究竟是真誠，還是品牌策略。

items.defEn: combine or unite to form one structure or organization
items.usage: 公司、族群、傳統皆可 amalgamate；語氣比 merge 稍書面。
items.exampleEn: The two clinics amalgamated to share laboratory equipment and staff.
items.exampleZh: 兩家診所合併，以共享實驗室設備與人力。

items.defEn: open to more than one interpretation; unclear
items.usage: GRE 常考「語意可兩解」，不一定等於「完全看不懂」（那更接近 obscure）。
items.exampleEn: The statute’s ambiguous wording invited years of litigation.
items.exampleZh: 該法條模稜兩可的措辭引發了多年訴訟。

items.defEn: the coexistence of conflicting feelings toward the same thing
items.usage: 不是「漠不關心」（apathy），而是同時喜歡又排斥；常接 toward/about。
items.exampleEn: Her ambivalence toward fame made her an uneasy public advocate.
items.exampleZh: 她對名聲的矛盾情感，使她成為心不甘情不願的公眾代言人。

items.defEn: make a bad condition better
items.usage: 對象多為問題、條件、關係；比 improve 更正式，且暗示原本不佳。
items.exampleEn: New irrigation methods ameliorated the soil’s salinity over several seasons.
items.exampleZh: 新的灌溉方法在數季內改善了土壤鹽化。

items.defEn: open and responsive to suggestion, authority, or influence
items.defZh: 順從的；可接受勸說的；願意配合的
items.usage: amenable to 為核心搭配；亦可表示「須受管轄／可被檢驗」。
items.exampleEn: The mayor was amenable to revising the zoning map after the hearing.
items.exampleZh: 聽證會後，市長願意配合修改分區地圖。

items.defEn: a pleasant or useful feature that adds comfort or convenience
items.defZh: 便利設施；舒適條件；禮儀
items.usage: 複數 amenities 最常見（公園、空調等）；單數亦可指禮貌、宜人特質。
items.exampleEn: The housing grant required each building to include basic amenities for residents.
items.exampleZh: 住房補助要求每棟建築為居民提供基本便利設施。

items.defEn: good-natured and likable
items.usage: 強調性格討喜；affable 偏重「好交談」，amiable 偏重「性情和善」。
items.exampleEn: An amiable moderator prevented the panel from dissolving into rivalry.
items.exampleZh: 親切的主持人避免座談淪為互相較勁。

items.defEn: lacking a definite shape, structure, or organization
items.usage: 可形容雲、組織、計畫；GRE 常批評論點或制度「散漫無形」。
items.exampleEn: The protest remained amorphous until a few demands crystallized into a platform.
items.exampleZh: 抗議活動一直結構模糊，直到若干訴求凝聚成綱領。

items.defEn: something placed in the wrong historical period; an outdated relic
items.usage: 可指文本中的史實錯誤，也可諷刺制度「跟不上時代」。
items.exampleEn: A rotary telephone in the otherwise futuristic set was a glaring anachronism.
items.exampleZh: 在整體未來感的場景中，轉盤電話成了刺眼的時代錯置。

items.defEn: comparable in certain respects, though otherwise different
items.usage: analogous to 為固定搭配；GRE 閱讀常用類比推理，未必表示完全相同。
items.exampleEn: The researcher argued that coral bleaching is analogous to fever in mammals.
items.exampleZh: 研究者主張，珊瑚白化可類比為哺乳動物發燒。

items.defEn: absence of government or order; chaotic disorder
items.usage: 政治義為「沒有統治」，日常引申為「一片混亂」；無政府主義者 anarchist 相關。
items.exampleEn: When the servers failed, the ticketing system descended into anarchy.
items.exampleZh: 伺服器故障後，售票系統陷入一片混亂。

items.defEn: based on isolated personal stories rather than systematic evidence
items.usage: GRE 科學段落常貶低 anecdotal evidence，對照 controlled data。
items.exampleEn: Anecdotal reports of recovery cannot substitute for a randomized trial.
items.exampleZh: 關於康復的軼事報導無法取代隨機試驗。

items.defEn: something that deviates from what is standard or expected
items.usage: 數據、氣候、行為皆可出現 anomaly；常觸發進一步調查。
items.exampleEn: The satellite detected a temperature anomaly over the polar ice.
items.exampleZh: 衛星在極地冰層上空偵測到溫度異常。

items.defEn: active hostility or opposition
items.usage: 可指人際仇恨，或藥物／化學上的拮抗作用；GRE 人文段多取「對立」。
items.exampleEn: Long-standing antagonism between the departments delayed the joint report.
items.exampleZh: 部門間長期的敵對拖延了聯合報告。

items.defEn: extremely old-fashioned; belonging to a time before the biblical flood
items.usage: 多帶嘲諷，形容觀念、設備「老掉牙」；字面「大洪水以前」較少單獨考。
items.exampleEn: The lab still relied on antediluvian filing cabinets instead of a digital archive.
items.exampleZh: 實驗室仍依賴過時的檔案櫃，而非數位典藏。

items.defEn: a deep-seated feeling of dislike
items.usage: 比 dislike 更深、更持久；常接 toward/for。勿與 apathy（冷漠）混淆。
items.exampleEn: Her antipathy toward speculative finance shaped the committee’s final rules.
items.exampleZh: 她對投機金融的反感，形塑了委員會的最終規範。

items.defEn: directly opposed or mutually incompatible
items.usage: antithetical to 為常見搭配；比 opposite 更強調「根本上不相容」。
items.exampleEn: Secret lobbying is antithetical to the transparency the charter demands.
items.exampleZh: 秘密遊說與章程所要求的透明完全對立。

items.defEn: lack of interest, concern, or emotion
items.usage: 政治、公民參與語境極常見；強調「沒感覺」，不是「討厭」。
items.exampleEn: Voter apathy, not opposition, was the campaign’s greatest obstacle.
items.exampleZh: 選民冷漠，而非反對力量，才是競選最大的障礙。

items.defEn: of doubtful authenticity; widely circulated but probably untrue
items.usage: 常修飾 anecdote、story、quotation；源自「次經」，GRE 取「不可靠」義。
items.exampleEn: The apocryphal tale of a midnight confession has never been documented.
items.exampleZh: 那段午夜懺悔的可疑傳聞從未被記錄證實。

items.defEn: calm or satisfy, especially by giving in to demands
items.usage: 可中性（平息怒氣），亦可貶義（以讓步換和平）；GRE 常帶負面評價。
items.exampleEn: Concessions meant to appease critics only invited further demands.
items.exampleZh: 本想安撫批評者的讓步，反而招來更多要求。

items.defEn: inform or notify someone of something
items.usage: 結構為 apprise someone of；勿與 appraise（評估）混淆，這是 GRE 經典陷阱。
items.exampleEn: Counsel failed to apprise the board of the looming lawsuit.
items.exampleZh: 法律顧問未能將迫在眉睫的訴訟告知董事會。

items.defEn: official or formal approval; warm praise
items.usage: 比 approval 更正式；常指公眾或權威的肯定。
items.exampleEn: The proposal won the dean’s approbation after a round of revisions.
items.exampleZh: 經過一輪修改後，該提案獲得院長認可。

items.defEn: take for one’s own use, often without permission; set aside for a purpose
items.usage: GRE 主考動詞「擅自取用」；國會語境亦可指「撥款」。形容詞「適當的」較少作為難題。
items.exampleEn: The curator was accused of appropriating indigenous designs without credit.
items.exampleZh: 策展人被指控未經標示就挪用原住民圖樣。

items.defEn: based on random choice or personal whim rather than reason or rule
items.usage: 法律與行政語境常批評 arbitrary power；不一定等於「隨機」，而是「缺乏正當標準」。
items.exampleEn: Students challenged the arbitrary penalties that varied from one instructor to another.
items.exampleZh: 學生質疑各教師輕重不一的武斷處罰。

items.defEn: understood by few; mysteriously obscure
items.defZh: 神秘難懂的；僅少數人知曉的
items.usage: 修飾規則、術語、儀式；帶「內行才懂」的距離感。
items.exampleEn: Only specialists could navigate the journal’s arcane citation conventions.
items.exampleZh: 只有專家才能摸清該期刊神秘難懂的引用慣例。

items.defEn: belonging to an earlier period; no longer in ordinary use
items.usage: 語言學指古語；制度批評中等於「不合時宜」。比 ancient 更強調「已廢棄」。
items.exampleEn: The contract still used archaic pronouns that confused modern readers.
items.exampleZh: 合約仍使用讓現代讀者困惑的古舊代名詞。

items.defEn: requiring strenuous effort; difficult and tiring
items.usage: 修飾 journey、task、process；強調耗力耗時，而非僅僅「複雜」。
items.exampleEn: Compiling the oral histories proved an arduous, decade-long project.
items.exampleZh: 彙編口述歷史成為一項耗時十年的艱鉅工程。

items.defEn: extremely dry; lacking interest or imagination
items.usage: 地理義「乾燥」與修辭義「乏味」GRE 皆考；arid prose 指文章乾巴巴。
items.exampleEn: The arid climate limited agriculture to a few irrigated valleys.
items.exampleZh: 乾旱氣候使農業僅能局限於少數灌溉河谷。

items.defEn: without guile; natural and unpretentious
items.usage: GRE 主考「不耍心機」，不是「沒有技藝」；後者偶爾出現，但較少成為正確義。
items.exampleEn: Her artless questions exposed contradictions the experts had politely ignored.
items.exampleZh: 她質樸無偽的提問，揭開了專家禮貌地忽略的矛盾。

items.defEn: practicing severe self-denial, especially for spiritual or moral reasons
items.usage: 可作名詞「苦行者」；勿與 aesthetic 混淆。強調主動克制，而非貧窮本身。
items.exampleEn: The founder’s ascetic habits clashed with the company’s later taste for luxury.
items.exampleZh: 創辦人的苦行習慣，與公司日後對奢華的品味衝突。

items.defEn: attribute a cause, quality, or origin to someone or something
items.usage: ascribe A to B；學術寫作極常見。與 attribute 近義。
items.exampleEn: Historians ascribe the city’s decline to silted harbors rather than invasion.
items.exampleZh: 史家將該城衰落歸因於港口淤積，而非入侵。

items.defEn: harshness of tone, temper, or conditions
items.usage: 可指說話尖刻，也可指氣候或環境嚴苛；with some asperity 常見於敘事。
items.exampleEn: She answered the interruption with asperity that silenced the room.
items.exampleZh: 她嚴厲地回應插話，使全場安靜下來。

items.defEn: attack violently, with words or force
items.usage: 對象可以是人、觀點或感官（assailed by doubts／odors）。
items.exampleEn: Opponents assailed the report as statistically unsound.
items.exampleZh: 反對者抨擊該報告在統計上站不住腳。

items.defEn: showing persistent and careful effort
items.usage: 正面詞；強調持續細心，而不只是忙碌。
items.exampleEn: Assiduous archival work uncovered letters the family had denied existed.
items.exampleZh: 勤勉的檔案工作找出了家族否認存在的信件。

items.defEn: make an unpleasant feeling less intense; satisfy an appetite
items.usage: 常見搭配 guilt、fears、hunger、grief；是減輕，不是徹底消除。
items.exampleEn: A public apology did little to assuage the community’s distrust.
items.exampleZh: 公開道歉幾乎無法緩和社區的不信任。

items.defEn: sharp or severe in manner; causing tissue to contract
items.usage: 醫學／化妝義為「收斂」；GRE 更常考評論語氣「尖銳苛刻」。
items.exampleEn: The editor’s astringent notes forced the author to cut every decorative clause.
items.exampleZh: 編輯嚴厲的批註迫使作者刪掉所有裝飾性子句。

items.defEn: shrewd and perceptive, especially in practical affairs
items.usage: 常修飾觀察、投資、政治判斷；帶讚賞色彩。
items.exampleEn: An astute reading of the footnotes revealed the study’s hidden funding source.
items.exampleZh: 敏銳地讀註腳，便揭示了研究隱藏的資金來源。

items.defEn: make amends for a wrong or injury
items.usage: atone for 為固定搭配；宗教與道德語境皆適用。
items.exampleEn: The company tried to atone for the spill by funding wetland restoration.
items.exampleZh: 公司試圖資助濕地復育，以彌補洩漏造成的傷害。

items.defEn: make thinner, weaker, or less effective
items.usage: 科學上可指訊號、病毒、光；論證上可指削弱主張的力度。
items.exampleEn: Distance attenuated the radio signal until only static remained.
items.exampleZh: 距離削弱了無線電訊號，直到只剩雜訊。

items.defEn: bold to the point of daring or impudence
items.usage: 可褒（有魄力）可貶（厚顏）；GRE 需依語境判斷作者態度。
items.exampleEn: The startup made an audacious bid to license the university’s entire patent portfolio.
items.exampleZh: 那家新創公司大膽競標授權大學的全部專利組合。

items.defEn: severely simple; stern in manner or appearance
items.usage: 可形容生活、風格、神情；與 luxury、ornament 對立。
items.exampleEn: The monastery’s austere rooms contained little more than a desk and a cot.
items.exampleZh: 修道院簡樸的房間幾乎只有一張書桌和一張窄床。

items.defEn: self-governing; acting independently
items.usage: 可指國家、機構、機器或個人；autonomy 為對應名詞。
items.exampleEn: The research institute remained autonomous despite relying on federal grants.
items.exampleZh: 儘管依賴聯邦補助，該研究所仍保持獨立自主。

items.defEn: extreme greed for wealth
items.usage: 語氣強烈且貶義；比 greed 更書面。
items.exampleEn: Prosecutors argued that avarice, not ideology, drove the insider trades.
items.exampleZh: 檢察官主張，驅使內線交易的是貪財，而非意識形態。

items.defEn: state confidently as a fact; assert
items.usage: 法律與學術語體常見；比 say 更強調「當作事實來主張」。
items.exampleEn: The witness averred that the documents had never left the locked cabinet.
items.exampleZh: 證人堅稱那些文件從未離開上鎖的櫃子。

items.defEn: showing keen interest or enthusiasm
items.usage: avid reader/collector 為高頻搭配；也可表示對金錢、權力的急切。
items.exampleEn: An avid collector of field notes, she digitized every surviving journal.
items.exampleZh: 作為熱衷蒐集田野筆記的人，她把所有倖存日記都數位化了。

items.defEn: declare openly and without shame
items.usage: 強調公開表態；avowed 常作形容詞，表示「公然的、自稱的」。
items.exampleEn: He avowed his opposition to the subsidy before the vote was called.
items.exampleZh: 在進入表決前，他公開表明反對該項補貼。

items.defEn: so lacking in originality as to be boring
items.usage: 強烈負評；GRE 寫作與文學評論中極常見。
items.exampleEn: The keynote collapsed into banal slogans that said nothing about the data.
items.exampleZh: 專題演講淪為對數據毫無說明的陳腐口號。

items.defEn: a cause of great distress or ruin
items.usage: the bane of 為固定結構；語氣戲劇化，可半開玩笑使用。
items.exampleEn: Unstable funding remained the bane of long-term ecological monitoring.
items.exampleZh: 不穩定的經費仍是長期生態監測的禍根。

items.defEn: fail to give a true impression of; contradict
items.usage: GRE 高頻：外表 belie 真實。不是 believe。
items.exampleEn: His calm tone belied the panic spreading through the trading floor.
items.exampleZh: 他平靜的語氣掩飾了交易大廳蔓延的恐慌。

items.defEn: make someone or something seem unimportant
items.usage: 帶明顯貶義；對象可以是成就、擔憂或人。
items.exampleEn: Senior partners belittled the intern’s proposal without reading the appendix.
items.exampleZh: 資深合夥人連附錄都沒讀就貶低實習生的提案。

items.defEn: demonstrating eagerness to fight or quarrel
items.usage: 比 aggressive 更書面；常修飾 rhetoric、nation、posture。
items.exampleEn: Bellicose speeches made diplomatic back channels nearly impossible.
items.exampleZh: 好戰的演說使私下外交管道幾乎無法運作。

items.defEn: hostile and aggressive; engaged in war
items.usage: 可指態度挑釁，或法律上的交戰國；名詞可指交戰方。
items.exampleEn: A belligerent questioner refused to let the witness finish a sentence.
items.exampleZh: 一名好鬥的提問者不讓證人把一句話說完。

items.defEn: a person who gives help or money, especially to an institution
items.usage: 博物館、大學語境高頻；不一定匿名，但常強調資助關係。
items.exampleEn: An anonymous benefactor underwrote the entire conservation laboratory.
items.exampleZh: 一位匿名捐助人承擔了整個修復實驗室的費用。

items.defEn: well-meaning and kindly; intending to do good
items.usage: 可修飾人、政策、專制（benevolent despot 為常見搭配，含諷刺可能）。
items.exampleEn: A benevolent grant program still imposed conditions that limited local control.
items.exampleZh: 一項出於善意的補助計畫仍附加了限制地方主導權的條件。

items.defEn: gentle and harmless; not malignant
items.usage: 醫學「良性」與氣候／影響「無害」皆考；對照 malignant、harmful。
items.exampleEn: What looked like a benign accounting change quietly inflated reported profits.
items.exampleZh: 看似無害的會計變更，悄悄地抬高了帳面獲利。

items.defEn: leave property or a legacy to someone by a will; pass down
items.usage: 法律義為遺囑贈與；引申為把傳統、問題留給後代。
items.exampleEn: She bequeathed her field notebooks to the university archive.
items.exampleZh: 她把田野筆記遺贈給大學檔案館。

items.defEn: scold or criticize angrily at length
items.usage: 語氣強，持續責罵；比 criticize 更情緒化。
items.exampleEn: The coach berated the squad for ignoring the safety briefing.
items.exampleZh: 教練痛責隊員無視安全簡報。

items.defEn: cause someone to become confused and uncertain
items.usage: past participle bewildered 極常見；強調混亂而非單純「不懂一個詞」。
items.exampleEn: Conflicting guidelines bewildered clinics trying to apply the new protocol.
items.exampleZh: 互相衝突的指引，讓試圖執行新程序的診所無所適從。

items.defEn: a thing that spoils, damages, or ruins; a plant disease
items.usage: 可作動詞「摧殘」；都市研究常見 urban blight（市容衰敗）。
items.exampleEn: Chronic disinvestment became a blight on once-thriving factory towns.
items.exampleZh: 長期缺乏投資，成了昔日繁榮工業小鎮的禍害。

items.defEn: support or strengthen; prop up
items.usage: 可指枕頭式支撐，更常引申為強化論點、信心、防線。
items.exampleEn: Additional citations were added to bolster the paper’s central claim.
items.exampleZh: 作者新增引用，以支撐論文的核心主張。

items.defEn: high-sounding but inflated and empty in language
items.defZh: 誇張空洞的；言過其實的
items.usage: 只評語言風格，不評爆炸；與 pompous 近。
items.exampleEn: Bombastic promises of a scientific revolution outpaced any actual results.
items.exampleZh: 對科學革命的誇張承諾，遠遠超過實際成果。

items.defEn: rude and insensitive in manners
items.usage: 強調教養差、不懂分寸；比 rude 更帶「沒文化」色彩。
items.exampleEn: Boorish interruptions made the seminar unusable for junior scholars.
items.exampleZh: 粗野的插話讓初級學者無法好好參與研討會。

items.defEn: characteristic of the conventional middle class, often in a materialistic way
items.defZh: 中產階級的；布爾喬亞的；世俗保守的
items.usage: 馬克思語境為階級標籤；文學批評中常帶「庸俗、安於現狀」的貶義。亦可作名詞。
items.exampleEn: The play mocked bourgeois taste without offering a coherent alternative.
items.exampleZh: 這齣戲嘲諷中產品味，卻拿不出前後一貫的替代方案。

items.defEn: a person who boasts annoyingly
items.usage: 明確貶義；動詞 brag 更常用，名詞強調「那種人」。
items.exampleEn: The panel had little patience for a braggart who cited no sources.
items.exampleZh: 對於不引來源只會吹噓的人，座談毫無耐心。

items.defEn: shamelessly bold; made of brass
items.usage: GRE 主考「公然無恥」；brazen it out 表示硬著頭皮撐下去。
items.exampleEn: The firm made a brazen attempt to patent a method already in the public domain.
items.exampleZh: 該公司厚顏地試圖為已屬公有領域的方法申請專利。

items.defEn: concise shortness of expression
items.usage: Brevity is the soul of wit 為成語；GRE 寫作亦褒獎 brevity。
items.exampleEn: The committee praised the brief for its brevity and precision.
items.exampleZh: 委員會稱讚這份陳述簡潔而精確。

items.defEn: tolerate or allow, especially an offense or delay
items.usage: GRE 主考動詞「容忍」，多用於否定：brook no interference。名詞「溪流」不是考點。
items.exampleEn: The editor would brook no sloppy citations in the final manuscript.
items.exampleZh: 編輯絕不容忍定稿中出現馬虎的引用。

items.defEn: relating to the pleasant aspects of country life
items.usage: 文學風格詞；可帶理想化色彩，不一定等於真實農村生活。
items.exampleEn: The novel’s bucolic opening contrasts sharply with its later industrial chapters.
items.exampleZh: 小說田園式的開場，與後來的工業章節形成鮮明對比。

items.defEn: grow or flourish rapidly
items.usage: burgeoning 常作形容詞；對象可以是產業、人口、興趣。
items.exampleEn: A burgeoning market in used lab equipment lowered start-up costs for new labs.
items.exampleZh: 二手實驗設備市場迅速成長，降低了新實驗室的啟動成本。

items.defEn: polish by rubbing; enhance a reputation
items.usage: GRE 常考引申義「打亮形象」；本義為金屬拋光。
items.exampleEn: The foundation funded scholarships mainly to burnish its public image.
items.exampleZh: 該基金會資助獎學金，主要是為了擦亮公眾形象。

items.defEn: give support or reinforcement to
items.usage: 建築本義為扶壁；GRE 多考「強化論點」。亦可作名詞。
items.exampleEn: Field interviews were used to buttress the statistical findings.
items.exampleZh: 田野訪談被用來支撐統計發現。

items.defEn: excessively complicated, secretive, or intrigue-ridden
items.defZh: 極其複雜的；詭譎繁複的
items.usage: 常小寫；諷刺官僚程序「迷宮般難懂」，不一定真與拜占庭史有關。
items.exampleEn: Byzantine procurement rules delayed even routine equipment orders.
items.exampleZh: 繁複詭譎的採購規則連例行設備訂單都拖慢了。

items.defEn: a harsh, discordant mixture of sounds
items.usage: 可指真實噪音，也可比喻意見衝突的「一片嘈雜」。
items.exampleEn: A cacophony of alarms made it impossible to isolate the real fault.
items.exampleZh: 一片刺耳的警報讓人無法找出真正的故障。

items.defEn: persuade by flattery or gentle coaxing
items.usage: 比 persuade 更強調「連哄帶騙」；常接 into。
items.exampleEn: She cajoled reluctant donors into attending the preview dinner.
items.exampleZh: 她連哄帶勸，讓不情願的捐助人出席預覽晚宴。

items.defEn: emotionally hardened; insensitive to others’ suffering
items.usage: 勿與 callus（繭）僅字形相近而混淆；GRE 考「沒有同情心」。
items.exampleEn: A callous cost-cutting memo ignored the layoffs’ effect on families.
items.exampleZh: 一封冷酷的成本刪減備忘錄，無視裁員對家庭的影響。

items.defEn: a false and malicious statement meant to damage a reputation
items.usage: 比 gossip 更惡意、更正式；動詞 calumniate 較罕見。
items.exampleEn: She sued the tabloid for calumny after it invented a plagiarism scandal.
items.exampleZh: 小報捏造抄襲醜聞後，她以誹謗為由提起訴訟。

items.defEn: frankness and sincerity in speech
items.usage: with candor 常見；正面詞，但有時「過度坦率」會傷人。
items.exampleEn: The auditor’s candor about missing receipts alarmed the trustees.
items.exampleZh: 審計人員對缺失收據的坦率發言，讓董事們感到震驚。

items.defEn: an accepted body of works or principles; a rule of judgment
items.usage: 文學「經典篇目」、宗教「正典」、一般「準則」皆考；canonical 為形容詞。
items.exampleEn: The course challenged the narrow canon of novels taught in previous decades.
items.exampleZh: 這門課挑戰了過去數十年所教授的狹窄小說經典名單。

items.defEn: bad-tempered, quarrelsome, and difficult to deal with
items.usage: 多形容老人、評論家、同事；語氣口語但 GRE 仍出現。
items.exampleEn: A cantankerous reviewer delayed publication with endless petty objections.
items.exampleZh: 一位脾氣暴躁的審稿人以沒完沒了的瑣碎反對拖延出版。

items.defEn: given to sudden, unpredictable changes of mood or behavior
items.usage: 可修飾人、天氣、政策；強調缺乏穩定原則。
items.exampleEn: Capricious funding cycles made it hard to retain trained technicians.
items.exampleZh: 反覆無常的經費週期，使訓練有素的技術人員難以留任。

items.defEn: eager to find trivial faults; overly critical
items.usage: 比 critical 更負面，強調「專找小毛病」。
items.exampleEn: Captious questions about commas distracted the committee from the paper’s thesis.
items.exampleZh: 對逗號吹毛求疵的提問，使委員會偏離了論文主題。

items.defEn: reprimand or punish severely
items.usage: 書面語；對象可以是人、政策或作品。
items.exampleEn: Editorial boards castigated the journal for hiding a conflict of interest.
items.exampleZh: 編輯委員會嚴厲譴責該期刊隱瞞利益衝突。

items.defEn: a person or event that precipitates change without being consumed by it
items.usage: 化學本義之外，GRE 更常考「加速變化的人或事件」。
items.exampleEn: The leak proved a catalyst for a complete overhaul of data security.
items.exampleZh: 這次外洩成了全面改革資料安全的催化劑。

items.defEn: able to burn or corrode; sharply sarcastic
items.usage: 科學義與修辭義皆考；caustic wit 指尖酸機智。
items.exampleEn: Her caustic aside about “peer review theater” circulated among graduate students.
items.exampleZh: 她對「同儕審查作秀」的刻薄旁白在研究生之間傳開。

items.defEn: express formal, often official, disapproval
items.usage: 亦可作名詞；比 criticize 更正式，常具公開或制度性。
items.exampleEn: The senate voted to censure the official for leaking confidential briefings.
items.exampleZh: 參議院投票譴責該官員洩漏機密簡報。

items.defEn: distress mixed with embarrassment at failure or humiliation
items.usage: to one’s chagrin 為高頻結構；強調「又氣又窘」。
items.exampleEn: To the inventor’s chagrin, a simpler device had already been patented.
items.exampleZh: 令發明人懊惱的是，更簡單的裝置早已取得專利。

items.defEn: a person who falsely claims knowledge or skill; a fraud
items.usage: 學術與醫療詐騙語境常見；比 liar 更聚焦「假專業」。
items.exampleEn: Investigators exposed the charlatan who sold untested “gene therapies.”
items.exampleZh: 調查人員揭穿了販售未經檢驗「基因療法」的騙子。

items.defEn: cautiously reluctant; wary
items.usage: chary of 為搭配；比 careful 更強調「捨不得／不敢輕易做」。
items.exampleEn: Investors remained chary of expanding until the legal risk was mapped.
items.exampleZh: 在法律風險釐清之前，投資人仍不輕易擴張。

items.defEn: clever but dishonest trickery, especially in legal or political matters
items.usage: 書面貶義；常指控程序、合約或選舉中的花樣。
items.exampleEn: The contract’s fine print was a masterpiece of legal chicanery.
items.exampleZh: 合約細則堪稱法律狡詐的傑作。

items.defEn: easily angered; hot-tempered
items.usage: 源自體液說的「膽汁質」；GRE 考性格「動輒發怒」。
items.exampleEn: A choleric supervisor made junior staff afraid to report equipment faults.
items.exampleZh: 暴躁的主管讓基層員工不敢回報設備故障。

items.defEn: longer than the most direct way; roundabout
items.usage: 可指道路或論證；circuitous reasoning 常含批評。
items.exampleEn: A circuitous argument buried the main claim under unnecessary history.
items.exampleZh: 迂迴的論證把主要主張埋在不必要的歷史之下。

items.defEn: restrict within limits; draw a line around
items.usage: GRE 多考「權力／自由被框住」；幾何「外接」義較少單獨成題。
items.exampleEn: Emergency statutes circumscribed the mayor’s spending authority.
items.exampleZh: 緊急法令限制了市長的支出權限。

items.defEn: careful to consider all circumstances before acting
items.usage: 強調「環顧四周再行動」；比 careful 更正式。
items.exampleEn: A circumspect diplomat refused to comment before verifying the cable.
items.exampleZh: 謹慎的外交官在核實電報前拒絕評論。

items.defEn: find a way around an obstacle or rule, often cleverly
items.usage: 可中性（繞開障礙）或貶義（鑽法律漏洞）。
items.exampleEn: Firms tried to circumvent export controls by routing parts through third countries.
items.exampleZh: 企業試圖經由第三國轉運零件，以規避出口管制。

items.defEn: supposedly able to perceive events beyond ordinary senses; unusually perceptive
items.defZh: 有洞察力的；有通靈預知的
items.usage: 字面「千里眼」常帶懷疑；比喻義為「看得極準」。亦可作名詞。
items.exampleEn: Her almost clairvoyant grasp of voter fatigue shaped the campaign’s quiet tone.
items.exampleZh: 她對選民疲乏近乎洞悉的掌握，形塑了競選的低調風格。

items.defEn: a loud, insistent outcry; noisy demand
items.usage: 亦可作動詞；a clamor for 表示公眾大聲要求。
items.exampleEn: A clamor for transparency followed the leaked budget spreadsheets.
items.exampleZh: 預算試算表外洩後，出現要求透明的鼓譟。

items.defEn: kept secret, especially because illicit
items.usage: 比 secret 更暗示「見不得光」；常修飾 meeting、operation、affair。
items.exampleEn: Clandestine testing of the compound violated the ethics protocol.
items.exampleZh: 對該化合物的暗中測試違反了倫理規範。

items.defEn: mercy, especially in reducing a punishment
items.usage: 法律語境高頻（presidential clemency）；也可泛指寬厚。
items.exampleEn: The governor granted clemency after new DNA evidence emerged.
items.exampleZh: 新的 DNA 證據出現後，州長給予寬赦。

items.defEn: come together to form one mass or whole
items.usage: 意見、團體、液滴皆可 coalesce；強調由分散變為一體。
items.exampleEn: Scattered complaints coalesced into a coherent reform agenda.
items.exampleZh: 零散的抱怨凝聚成前後一貫的改革議程。

items.defEn: gently persuade someone to do something
items.usage: 語氣比 cajole 稍中性；也可指小心引出資料或機器運轉。
items.exampleEn: Technicians coaxed the aging telescope through one last observation night.
items.exampleZh: 技術人員耐心哄著老化的望遠鏡完成最後一夜觀測。

items.defEn: compel by force, threats, or pressure
items.usage: 與 coax 對立；法律上 coercion 可推翻同意的效力。
items.exampleEn: No participant may be coerced into remaining in the clinical trial.
items.exampleZh: 任何參與者都不得被脅迫繼續留在臨床試驗中。

items.defEn: clear, logical, and convincing
items.defZh: 有說服力的；論點中肯的
items.usage: 幾乎只修飾 argument、case、reason；GRE 寫作高頻正面詞。
items.exampleEn: A cogent dissent forced the majority to address the sampling bias.
items.exampleZh: 一份有力的異議意見，迫使多數意見回應抽樣偏差。

items.defEn: aware of and having knowledge about something
items.usage: cognizant of 為固定搭配；正式書面語。
items.exampleEn: The board was cognizant of the conflict but delayed disclosure.
items.exampleZh: 董事會察覺到利益衝突，卻延後揭露。

items.defEn: in proportion; matching in degree or size
items.usage: commensurate with 為核心搭配；薪資、懲罰、風險常與此詞連用。
items.exampleEn: The penalty was not commensurate with the harm done to patients.
items.exampleZh: 該處罰與對病人造成的傷害並不相稱。

items.defEn: evoking strong interest or conviction; not easy to ignore
items.defZh: 令人信服的；引人注目的
items.usage: 可指論證有力，或故事／證據讓人無法忽視。
items.exampleEn: Compelling satellite images left little doubt that the glacier had retreated.
items.exampleZh: 令人信服的衛星影像幾乎不容置疑冰川已經後退。

items.defEn: self-satisfied to the point of unawareness of danger or flaw
items.usage: GRE 經典陷阱：不是 complaisant（討好的）。帶負評。
items.exampleEn: Complacent incumbents underestimated a poorly funded challenger.
items.exampleZh: 自滿的現任者低估了資金不足的挑戰者。

items.defEn: willing to please others; obliging
items.defZh: 殷勤討好的；順從他人的
items.usage: 與 complacent 僅差一字；強調「好說話、願意配合」，有時暗示缺乏主見。
items.exampleEn: A complaisant assistant never questioned even dubious travel claims.
items.exampleZh: 一位殷勤討好的助理，連可疑的差旅報銷也不質疑。

items.defEn: combining so as to complete or enhance each other
items.usage: 勿與 complimentary（免費的／恭維的）混淆；GRE 常設此陷阱。
items.exampleEn: Qualitative interviews proved complementary to the large-scale survey.
items.exampleZh: 質性訪談與大規模調查形成互補。

items.defEn: inclined to agree or obey; meeting official standards
items.usage: 人可「順從」，產品／程序可「符合規定」（regulatory compliant）。
items.exampleEn: The laboratory remained compliant with biosafety rules after the inspection.
items.exampleZh: 檢查後，實驗室仍符合生物安全規定。

items.defEn: involved with others in wrongdoing
items.usage: complicit in 為搭配；不一定親自動手，知情放任也可算。
items.exampleEn: Officials who ignored the falsified logs were complicit in the fraud.
items.exampleZh: 對偽造紀錄視而不見的官員，等於共謀欺詐。

items.defEn: intended to soothe anger and restore goodwill
items.usage: 修飾 tone、gesture、offer；與 belligerent 對立。
items.exampleEn: A conciliatory letter reopened talks that had stalled for months.
items.exampleZh: 一封和解信使停滯數月的談判重新展開。

items.defEn: occurring or existing at the same time, often as a result
items.usage: 亦可作名詞；強調「伴隨而來」，不一定有因果，但常暗示相關。
items.exampleEn: Rapid urbanization brought concomitant strains on water systems.
items.exampleZh: 快速都市化伴隨而來的是供水系統的壓力。

items.defEn: treat a wrong as if it were acceptable; overlook
items.usage: 不是「原諒並修復」，而是「當作可以接受」；常含批評。
items.exampleEn: The university would not condone plagiarism even in first-year courses.
items.exampleZh: 即使在一年級課程，大學也不會縱容抄襲。

items.defEn: cause surprise and confusion; mix up; refute
items.usage: 統計上 confounding variable 為干擾變項；亦可表示「打臉預期」。
items.exampleEn: The results confounded experts who had predicted a sharp decline.
items.exampleZh: 結果使預期會急遽下降的專家感到困惑。

items.defEn: pleasant because suited to one’s tastes or nature
items.usage: 可指人合得來，或環境適合；與 congenital（先天的）勿混。
items.exampleEn: She found the archive’s quiet routine congenial to careful scholarship.
items.exampleZh: 她覺得檔案館安靜的日常，很適合嚴謹的學術工作。

items.defEn: an opinion formed without sufficient evidence
items.usage: 亦可作動詞；academic 語境常對照 evidence、proof。
items.exampleEn: Without core samples, claims about the lake’s origin remain conjecture.
items.exampleZh: 沒有岩芯樣本，關於該湖起源的說法仍只是推測。

items.defEn: an expert judge in matters of taste, especially the arts or food
items.usage: 帶品味與專業判斷；不一定是創作者。
items.exampleEn: A connoisseur of early maps spotted the forged coastline at once.
items.exampleZh: 一位早期地圖鑑賞家立刻看出偽造的海岸線。

items.defEn: make or declare sacred; devote to a solemn purpose
items.usage: 宗教儀式之外，也可表示把生命或場所獻給崇高目標。
items.exampleEn: The hall was consecrated as a memorial to workers lost in the collapse.
items.exampleZh: 大廳被奉獻為倒塌事故中罹難工人的紀念場所。

items.defEn: general agreement among a group
items.usage: 不要求百分之百同意，而是廣泛一致；scientific consensus 為高頻搭配。
items.exampleEn: No consensus emerged on how to weight qualitative evidence.
items.exampleZh: 對於如何加權質性證據，並未形成共識。

items.defEn: clearly visible; attracting notice, sometimes uncomfortably
items.usage: 可中性（明顯）或負面（太招搖）；conspicuous consumption 為固定術語。
items.exampleEn: The error was conspicuous in the opening table, yet no one corrected it.
items.exampleZh: 錯誤在開篇表格中十分顯眼，卻沒有人改正。

items.defEn: sudden anxiety and dismay, often causing confusion
items.usage: to one’s consternation；比 surprise 更帶「不知所措」。
items.exampleEn: The unexpected resignation caused consternation among coalition partners.
items.exampleZh: 突如其來的辭職讓聯盟夥伴驚愕不安。

items.defEn: a limitation or restriction; the state of being restricted
items.usage: budget/time constraints 極常見；亦可指舉止拘束。
items.exampleEn: Ethical constraints forbade paying subjects for political endorsements.
items.exampleZh: 倫理約束禁止付錢請受試者做政治背書。

items.defEn: assert in an argument; compete or struggle
items.usage: GRE 兩義皆考：contend that（主張）與 contend with/for（對抗／爭奪）。
items.exampleEn: The authors contend that the sample underrepresents rural clinics.
items.exampleZh: 作者主張該樣本低估了鄉村診所的比例。

items.defEn: causing or likely to cause disagreement; quarrelsome
items.usage: 可修飾議題或性格；contentious issue 為閱讀高頻。
items.exampleEn: A contentious clause on data ownership stalled the collaboration agreement.
items.exampleZh: 一條關於資料所有權的爭議條款，使合作協議停滯。

items.defEn: dependent on something else that may or may not happen
items.usage: contingent on/upon 為搭配；亦可作名詞「代表團、分隊」。GRE 主考形容詞。
items.exampleEn: Final approval was contingent on a successful environmental review.
items.exampleZh: 最終批准取決於環境審查是否通過。

items.defEn: feeling or showing sincere remorse
items.usage: 強調真心悔過，而非表面道歉；contrition 為名詞。
items.exampleEn: A contrite statement still failed to explain how the data were altered.
items.exampleZh: 一份悔悟聲明仍然沒有解釋資料是如何被改動的。

items.defEn: artificially created and therefore unconvincing
items.defZh: 不自然的；牽強的；刻意安排的
items.usage: 文學與情節批評高頻；暗示「做作、假」。
items.exampleEn: The novel’s ending felt contrived, as if a moral had been bolted on.
items.exampleZh: 小說結局顯得牽強，彷彿硬接上一則道德教訓。

items.defEn: a confusing and difficult problem or question
items.usage: 比 problem 更強調「兩難或費解」；可指謎語本身。
items.exampleEn: Balancing open data with patient privacy remains a policy conundrum.
items.exampleZh: 在開放資料與病人隱私之間取得平衡，仍是政策難題。

items.defEn: based on accepted custom or standard practice
items.defZh: 傳統的；慣例的；墨守成規的
items.usage: 可中性（常規療法）或貶義（缺乏創見）；conventional wisdom 常被挑戰。
items.exampleEn: The study questioned conventional wisdom about calorie counting.
items.exampleZh: 該研究質疑關於熱量計算的傳統看法。

items.defEn: move toward the same point or conclusion
items.usage: 道路、意見、證據皆可 converge；對應 diverge。
items.exampleEn: Independent studies converged on the same causal mechanism.
items.exampleZh: 獨立研究匯聚到相同的因果機制。

items.defEn: friendly, lively, and fond of company and festivity
items.defZh: 歡快友善的；愛好宴樂的
items.usage: 修飾氣氛、聚會、性格；比 sociable 更帶「一起吃喝談笑」色彩。
items.exampleEn: A convivial dinner did more to settle the dispute than a formal memo.
items.exampleZh: 一場歡快的晚餐，比正式備忘錄更能化解爭端。

items.defEn: extremely complex and difficult to follow
items.defZh: 錯綜複雜的；晦澀曲折的
items.usage: 常批評句子、情節、法規「繞來繞去」；本義為捲曲。
items.exampleEn: Convoluted footnotes obscured rather than supported the main argument.
items.exampleZh: 錯綜複雜的註腳掩蓋了主論，而非支撐它。

items.defEn: abundant in quantity
items.usage: copious notes/evidence/tears 為常見搭配。
items.exampleEn: The intern took copious notes but struggled to rank their importance.
items.exampleZh: 實習生做了大量筆記，卻難以排出重要性。

items.defEn: confirm or give support to a statement or finding
items.usage: 證據互相 corroborate；法庭與科學寫作高頻。
items.exampleEn: Satellite data corroborated the villagers’ accounts of night-time flooding.
items.exampleZh: 衛星資料證實了村民關於夜間淹水的陳述。

items.defEn: familiar with and at ease in many cultures; worldly and international
items.usage: 可修飾城市、態度、人；亦可作名詞「世界公民」。
items.exampleEn: A cosmopolitan faculty made the seminar unusually comparative in method.
items.exampleZh: 一批見多識廣的師資，使研討會在方法上異常具比較性。

items.defEn: admit as acceptable or possible; give support or approval to
items.usage: GRE 主考動詞「容忍／贊同」；名詞「面容」較直白，常作干擾義。
items.exampleEn: The dean would not countenance secret recording of faculty meetings.
items.exampleZh: 院長不容許祕密錄製教師會議。

items.defEn: a sudden, successful seizure of power; a brilliant, unexpected success
items.defZh: 政變；漂亮的一擊；大成功
items.usage: coup d’état 為政變；a publicity coup 指宣傳上的漂亮成果。
items.exampleEn: Winning the archive’s exclusive rights was a scholarly coup for the museum.
items.exampleZh: 贏得檔案獨家權利，是博物館學術上的漂亮一擊。

items.defEn: not openly acknowledged or displayed
items.usage: 與 overt 成對；情報、偏見、行動皆可 covert。
items.exampleEn: Covert funding of the petition undermined claims of grassroots support.
items.exampleZh: 對請願的暗中資助，削弱了「基層支持」的說法。

items.defEn: yearn to possess something belonging to someone else
items.usage: 帶道德貶義較多；coveted 常作「令人垂涎的」。
items.exampleEn: Rival labs coveted the rare tissue samples stored in the freezer.
items.exampleZh: 對手實驗室覬覦冷凍庫中稀有的組織樣本。

items.defEn: crouch or shrink back in fear
items.usage: 強調害怕而身體退縮；比 hesitate 更具體、更貶或更可憐。
items.exampleEn: Staff cowered during the outburst instead of documenting the safety violation.
items.exampleZh: 主管爆發時員工紛紛畏縮，而沒有記錄這次安全違規。

items.defEn: contemptibly lacking in courage
items.usage: 強烈貶義；比 cowardly 更書面。亦可作名詞。
items.exampleEn: Critics called the retraction a craven attempt to appease donors.
items.exampleZh: 批評者稱這次撤稿是為安撫捐款人而做出的怯懦之舉。

items.defEn: too ready to believe, even on weak evidence
items.usage: 勿與 credible（可信的）或 incredulous（不相信的）混淆。
items.exampleEn: Credulous investors poured money into a company with no audited statements.
items.exampleZh: 輕信的投資人把錢投入一家沒有經審計報表的公司。

items.defEn: a standard by which something is judged
items.usage: 單數 criterion，複數 criteria；GRE 常考單複數錯誤。
items.exampleEn: Statistical significance was not the sole criterion for publication.
items.exampleZh: 統計顯著性並非唯一的發表標準。

items.defEn: having a hidden or obscure meaning
items.usage: 修飾訊息、微笑、註解；強調「費解且似有深意」。
items.exampleEn: A cryptic footnote hinted at data the authors declined to share.
items.exampleZh: 一則隱晦的註腳暗示了作者拒絕分享的資料。

items.defEn: reach a climax or final, decisive point
items.usage: culminate in 為搭配；表示過程走到最高或最終階段。
items.exampleEn: Years of quiet mapping culminated in a public atlas of flood risk.
items.exampleZh: 多年默默測繪，最終成就一份公開的洪水風險地圖集。

items.defEn: deserving blame
items.usage: legal 語境常見；culpability 為名詞。程度可輕於 criminal。
items.exampleEn: The report found the contractor culpable for skipping required inspections.
items.exampleZh: 報告認定承包商因跳過必要檢查而應受責備。

items.defEn: large, heavy, or complicated and therefore hard to handle
items.usage: 可指物體沉重，或程序、句子「累贅」。
items.exampleEn: A cumbersome approval chain delayed every software patch.
items.exampleZh: 繁瑣的核准鏈拖慢了每一次軟體修補。

items.defEn: greedy desire for wealth
items.usage: 與 avarice 近義，書面且貶；不一定含暴力，聚焦金錢欲。
items.exampleEn: The fraud was driven less by ideology than by simple cupidity.
items.exampleZh: 這起詐騙與其說出於意識形態，不如說出於單純貪財。

items.defEn: hasty and not thorough
items.usage: cursory glance/review 為高頻；暗示因快而漏看。
items.exampleEn: A cursory reading of the appendix would have revealed the missing control group.
items.exampleZh: 只要粗略讀過附錄，就會發現缺少控制組。

items.defEn: distrustful of others’ motives; believing people act from self-interest
items.defZh: 憤世嫉俗的；懷疑動機的
items.usage: 可指看穿虛偽，也可貶為「一味以惡意度人」。
items.exampleEn: A cynical public assumed the apology was timed for the stock offering.
items.exampleZh: 憤世的公眾認定這份道歉是配合股票發行時程。

items.defEn: make someone feel intimidated or discouraged
items.usage: undaunted 極常見；daunting task 為高頻形容詞用法。
items.exampleEn: The scale of the cleanup did not daunt the volunteer engineers.
items.exampleZh: 清理工程的規模並未讓志願工程師氣餒。

items.defEn: a scarcity or lack of something
items.usage: a dearth of 為固定結構；比 lack 更書面。
items.exampleEn: A dearth of bilingual reviewers slowed the journal’s special issue.
items.exampleZh: 缺乏雙語審稿人，拖慢了期刊特刊進度。

items.defEn: a sudden and ignominious failure; a complete collapse
items.usage: 語氣強，帶難堪；可用於軍事、市場、專案。
items.exampleEn: The product launch became a debacle after the app erased user data.
items.exampleZh: 應用程式刪除使用者資料後，產品發表會變成一場慘敗。

items.defEn: make weak or infirm
items.usage: 可指疾病使人虛弱，或政策／壓力削弱機構能力。
items.exampleEn: Chronic understaffing debilitated the clinic’s emergency response.
items.exampleZh: 長期人手不足削弱了診所的緊急應變能力。

items.defEn: behavior in keeping with good taste and propriety
items.usage: courtroom/academic decorum 常見；強調公開場合的分寸。
items.exampleEn: The judge demanded a minimum of decorum even during heated objections.
items.exampleZh: 即使在激烈異議時，法官仍要求最基本的禮儀。

items.defEn: failure to fulfill an obligation, especially a payment; a preset option
items.usage: 金融「違約」與電腦「預設」皆可能出現；by default 可指「因對方缺席／未作為」。
items.exampleEn: The city’s default on bond payments triggered an immediate downgrade.
items.exampleZh: 該市拖欠債券付款，立即引發評等下調。

items.defEn: respectful submission to another’s judgment or status
items.usage: in deference to 為高頻；比 respect 更強調「讓步、聽從」。
items.exampleEn: In deference to local historians, the plaque text was rewritten.
items.exampleZh: 出於對當地史家的敬重，牌匾文字被重寫。

items.defEn: no longer existing, living, or operating
items.defZh: 已不存在的；停業的；失效的
items.usage: 修飾公司、制度、雜誌；語氣比 outdated 更徹底「已經沒了」。
items.exampleEn: Grant money sat unused in the account of a defunct research center.
items.exampleZh: 補助款閒置在一家已停運研究中心的帳戶裡。

items.defEn: causing harm or damage
items.usage: 書面語，常修飾 effects、impact；科學與政策段落高頻。
items.exampleEn: Even low-level exposure had deleterious effects on memory tests.
items.exampleZh: 即使低劑量暴露，仍對記憶測驗造成有害影響。

items.defEn: describe or portray precisely; mark the outline of
items.usage: 可指畫出邊界，或精確說明職責、論點。
items.exampleEn: The charter delineates the ombudsman’s powers with unusual clarity.
items.exampleZh: 章程異常清晰地劃定了申訴專員的權限。

items.defEn: outward behavior or bearing
items.usage: 強調外在給人的印象，不一定等於內心。
items.exampleEn: Her calm demeanor at the hearing contrasted with the angry emails she had sent.
items.exampleZh: 她在聽證會上的平靜舉止，與她先前憤怒的電子郵件形成對比。

items.defEn: criticize unfairly; belittle the reputation of
items.usage: 比 criticize 更不公平、更具攻擊性；書面貶義。
items.exampleEn: Rivals denigrated the vaccine study without engaging its methods.
items.exampleZh: 對手並未討論其方法，便詆毀這項疫苗研究。

items.defEn: an inhabitant or regular occupant of a place
items.usage: 可指人或動物；語氣略文學，不一定有法律公民身分。
items.exampleEn: Foxes had become denizens of the abandoned rail yards.
items.exampleZh: 狐狸已成為廢棄鐵路場的常駐居民。

items.defEn: publicly declare to be wrong or evil
items.usage: 語氣公開且強烈；可針對政策、暴行或個人。
items.exampleEn: Civil-rights groups denounced the ordinance as a disguised travel ban.
items.exampleZh: 民權團體公開譴責該條例實為變相旅行禁令。

items.defEn: use up or reduce the amount of something
items.usage: 資源、存款、體力皆可 deplete；depleted 常作形容詞。
items.exampleEn: Overfishing had depleted stocks that once supported the coastal towns.
items.exampleZh: 過度捕撈已耗盡一度支撐沿海城鎮的魚群。

items.defEn: feel or express strong disapproval of
items.usage: 正式語，常用於社論與學術討論中的道德判斷。
items.exampleEn: Historians deplore the destruction of the archives during the conflict.
items.exampleZh: 史家強烈譴責衝突期間檔案遭毀。

items.defEn: remove from a high office or position of power
items.usage: 政治與歷史文本常見；受詞多為統治者或高官。
items.exampleEn: Parliament voted to depose the minister after the inquiry.
items.exampleZh: 國會在調查後表決罷免該部長。

items.defEn: moral corruption; extreme wickedness
items.usage: 語氣極重，指道德上的敗壞而非一般缺點。
items.exampleEn: The memoir exposed the depravity behind the charity’s public image.
items.exampleZh: 回憶錄揭露該慈善機構公開形象背後的墮落。

items.defEn: express mild but firm disapproval of
items.usage: GRE 勿與 depreciate（貶值）混淆；語氣比 condemn 溫和。
items.exampleEn: Several reviewers deprecate the study’s reliance on anecdotal evidence.
items.exampleZh: 數位評審對該研究倚賴軼事證據表示不以為然。

items.defEn: mock with contempt
items.usage: 帶輕蔑色彩，比 tease 更具敵意。
items.exampleEn: Critics deride the proposal as a publicity stunt rather than a reform.
items.exampleZh: 批評者譏諷該提案只是作秀，而非真正改革。

items.defEn: unoriginal; taken from something already existing
items.usage: GRE 多考「抄襲感／不創新」，作負面評價。
items.exampleEn: The novel is technically polished but painfully derivative of earlier dystopias.
items.exampleZh: 這部小說技法圓熟，卻明顯沿襲先前的反烏托邦作品。

items.defEn: dry out thoroughly; drain of vitality
items.usage: 可指字面乾燥，亦可比喻抽空生命力或趣味。
items.exampleEn: Years of budget cuts have desiccated the once-vibrant research program.
items.exampleZh: 多年預算刪減已使昔日蓬勃的研究計畫枯竭。

items.defEn: in low spirits from loss of hope
items.usage: 強調因希望落空而消沉，常見 collocation：despondent over。
items.exampleEn: The team grew despondent after three consecutive failed trials.
items.exampleZh: 連續三次試驗失敗後，團隊變得沮喪。

items.defEn: a ruler with absolute and often oppressive power
items.usage: 歷史與政治評論用語；形容詞為 despotic。
items.exampleEn: The despot silenced universities that questioned official statistics.
items.exampleZh: 那位暴君壓制質疑官方數據的大學。

items.defEn: lacking a plan or purpose; jumping from one thing to another
items.usage: GRE 常考「缺乏系統」，不是「侮辱的」。
items.exampleEn: The committee’s desultory discussion produced no usable recommendation.
items.exampleZh: 委員會漫無章法的討論未能產出可用建議。

items.defEn: emotionally uninvolved; standing apart
items.usage: 可褒（客觀冷靜）可貶（冷漠疏離），視語境而定。
items.exampleEn: A detached observer can weigh the testimony without taking sides.
items.exampleZh: 超然的觀察者能不偏不倚地衡量證詞。

items.defEn: something that discourages or prevents an action
items.usage: 政策與法律文本常見；亦可作形容詞。
items.exampleEn: Higher fines proved a weak deterrent against illegal dumping.
items.exampleZh: 更高罰款對非法棄置的威懾效果薄弱。

items.defEn: a bitter, abusive verbal attack
items.usage: 指長篇激烈指責，語域偏正式或文學。
items.exampleEn: His op-ed degenerated into a diatribe against the entire profession.
items.exampleZh: 他的評論專欄淪為對整個行業的痛罵。

items.defEn: a division into two sharply contrasting parts
items.usage: 學術寫作常用 false dichotomy（錯誤二分法）提醒過度簡化。
items.exampleEn: The study rejects a strict dichotomy between nature and culture.
items.exampleZh: 該研究否定自然與文化之間的嚴格二分。

items.defEn: intended to instruct, often in a preachy way
items.usage: 中性可指「具教育性」，負面則指「好為人師」。
items.exampleEn: The film is informative, yet its didactic tone alienates adult viewers.
items.exampleZh: 這部影片資訊豐富，但說教語氣疏遠了成年觀眾。

items.defEn: lacking self-confidence; timid in asserting oneself
items.usage: GRE 勿與 different 聯想；指態度畏縮而非「不同」。
items.exampleEn: Even the most diffident speaker improved after structured coaching.
items.exampleZh: 即使最羞怯的講者也在系統指導後有所進步。

items.defEn: spread out; wordy and lacking focus
items.defZh: 散漫的；冗長而不集中的
items.usage: GRE 常考「文章鬆散冗贅」；亦可作動詞「擴散」。
items.exampleEn: The argument is learned but too diffuse to persuade a skeptical panel.
items.exampleZh: 論點頗有學養，卻過於散漫，難以說服存疑的評審團。

items.defEn: stray from the main topic
items.usage: 學術口語常見 if I may digress；名詞為 digression。
items.exampleEn: The lecturer began to digress into personal anecdotes unrelated to the data.
items.exampleZh: 講師開始離題，轉而講述與數據無關的個人軼事。

items.defEn: slow to act; intended to cause delay
items.usage: 法律與行政語境常見 dilatory tactics（拖延戰術）。
items.exampleEn: Dilatory filing of the report delayed the entire audit cycle.
items.exampleZh: 報告拖延提交，使整個稽核週期延後。

items.defEn: a person who dabbles in a field without serious commitment
items.defZh: 淺嘗輒止者；業餘愛好者
items.usage: 多帶貶義，暗示不夠專業；亦可作形容詞。
items.exampleEn: Serious botanists dismissed him as a dilettante with a photogenic garden.
items.exampleZh: 嚴謹的植物學家視他為徒有上鏡花園的淺嘗者。

items.defEn: showing careful and persistent effort
items.usage: 正面評價；常見 diligent research / diligent student。
items.exampleEn: Diligent archival work uncovered letters the biography had missed.
items.exampleZh: 勤勉的檔案考據找出傳記遺漏的書信。

items.defEn: a reduction in size, extent, or importance
items.usage: 正式名詞，常接 of 表示被削弱的事物。
items.exampleEn: The court noted a diminution of public trust after the leaks.
items.exampleZh: 法院指出洩密後公眾信任有所減損。

items.defEn: a mournful song or poem, especially for the dead
items.usage: 可字面指喪禮歌曲，亦可比喻氣氛極度哀傷的作品。
items.exampleEn: The final movement sounds less like a symphony than a dirge.
items.exampleZh: 末樂章聽來不像交響曲，倒像一首輓歌。

items.defEn: free someone from a mistaken belief
items.usage: 固定搭配 disabuse someone of an idea；字面與 abuse 無關。
items.exampleEn: The data should disabuse investors of the notion that the market cannot fall.
items.exampleZh: 這些數據應使投資人醒悟市場不可能下跌的迷思。

items.defEn: perceive or distinguish clearly, often with insight
items.usage: 強調細微差別的判斷力；形容詞為 discerning。
items.exampleEn: A trained editor can discern tone shifts that casual readers miss.
items.exampleZh: 訓練有素的編輯能辨識普通讀者忽略的語氣轉變。

items.defEn: unsettle or throw into confusion
items.usage: 過去分詞 disconcerted 常用來形容被打亂節奏的人。
items.exampleEn: An unexpected question from the chair disconcerted the otherwise calm witness.
items.exampleZh: 主席突如其來的提問使原本沉著的證人慌亂。

items.defEn: conflicting; harsh or inharmonious
items.usage: 可指聲音刺耳，亦可指意見或數據互相衝突。
items.exampleEn: The two agencies released discordant estimates of the same outbreak.
items.exampleZh: 兩機構對同一疫情發布了相互抵觸的估計。

items.defEn: harm the reputation of; cause to be doubted
items.defZh: 使名譽受損；使不足採信
items.usage: 學術與新聞常見 discredit a theory / a source。
items.exampleEn: Forged citations were enough to discredit the entire paper.
items.exampleZh: 偽造的引用足以使整篇論文失去可信度。

items.defEn: a difference between facts or claims that should agree
items.usage: 審計與研究寫作高頻詞；常接 between A and B。
items.exampleEn: Auditors flagged a discrepancy between reported hours and badge records.
items.exampleZh: 稽核人員標出申報工時與門禁紀錄之間的出入。

items.defEn: separate and distinct; individually detached
items.usage: GRE 必考與 discreet（謹慎）的拼寫陷阱。
items.exampleEn: The model treats each household as a discrete decision-making unit.
items.exampleZh: 該模型將每個家戶視為分立的決策單位。

items.defEn: the freedom to decide; prudent reserve in speech or action
items.usage: at someone’s discretion 指由某人自行決定；亦指守口如瓶。
items.exampleEn: Hiring bonuses were left to the director’s discretion.
items.exampleZh: 聘用獎金交由主任裁量。

items.defEn: a feeling that someone or something is unworthy of respect
items.usage: 可作動詞；常見 treat with disdain / disdain for。
items.exampleEn: She spoke of marketing slogans with undisguised disdain.
items.exampleZh: 她談及行銷口號時毫不掩飾輕蔑。

items.defEn: not candid; pretending to be naive or sincere
items.usage: GRE 常考「裝無辜」；反義 ingenuous 才是天真率直。
items.exampleEn: It is disingenuous to claim surprise after months of internal warnings.
items.exampleZh: 在內部預警數月之後仍稱感到驚訝，並不誠實。

items.defEn: impartial; free from selfish bias
items.defZh: 公正無私的；不涉利害的
items.usage: GRE 必考「公正」，勿與 uninterested（不感興趣）混淆。
items.exampleEn: The mediation needs a disinterested chair with no financial stake.
items.exampleZh: 調解需要一位毫無財務利害的公正主席。

items.defEn: lacking coherent connection; disconnected
items.usage: 常修飾 speech, narrative, argument。
items.exampleEn: The witness offered a disjointed account that jumped across years.
items.exampleZh: 證人的陳述支離破碎，時間前後跳躍。

items.defEn: speak of as having little worth; belittle
items.usage: 正式語；常見 disparage someone’s efforts / credentials。
items.exampleEn: Senior partners should not disparage junior research in public meetings.
items.exampleZh: 資深合夥人不宜在公開會議上貶低初級研究。

items.defEn: fundamentally distinct or unequal
items.usage: 勿與 desperate 混淆；常修飾 groups, findings, sources。
items.exampleEn: The report tries to reconcile disparate datasets collected over decades.
items.exampleZh: 報告試圖調和數十年間收集的迥異資料集。

items.defEn: not influenced by strong emotion; calm and fair
items.defZh: 冷靜客觀的；不動感情的
items.usage: 正面多指判斷不受情緒左右，適合學術與司法語境。
items.exampleEn: A dispassionate review of the fatalities changed the safety protocol.
items.exampleZh: 對死亡案例的冷靜檢視改變了安全規程。

items.defEn: speed and efficiency in carrying out a task
items.usage: GRE 常考 with dispatch（迅速辦妥）；亦可作動詞「派遣」。
items.exampleEn: The emergency team restored power with impressive dispatch.
items.exampleZh: 緊急小組以驚人的速度恢復供電。

items.defEn: drive away doubts, fears, or illusions
items.usage: 受詞多為抽象事物：myths, rumors, fears。
items.exampleEn: Transparent sampling methods helped dispel doubts about the poll.
items.exampleZh: 透明的抽樣方法有助消除對民調的疑慮。

items.defEn: scatter in different directions
items.usage: 可指人群散去，亦可指物質或資金分散。
items.exampleEn: Police asked the crowd to disperse after the announcement.
items.exampleZh: 警方在宣布後要求群眾散去。

items.defEn: conceal one’s true motives or feelings
items.usage: GRE 勿與 disassemble（拆卸）混淆。
items.exampleEn: Experienced diplomats can dissemble without uttering a direct falsehood.
items.exampleZh: 老練的外交官能在不直接說謊的情況下掩飾真意。

items.defEn: spread widely, especially information or ideas
items.usage: 學術與公共衛生高頻詞：disseminate findings / guidelines。
items.exampleEn: The agency moved quickly to disseminate the revised safety guidelines.
items.exampleZh: 該機構迅速傳播修訂後的安全指引。

items.defEn: withhold agreement; differ in opinion
items.usage: 法律常見 dissenting opinion；亦可作名詞。
items.exampleEn: Two justices dissent from the majority on the scope of the statute.
items.exampleZh: 兩位大法官對該法條適用範圍與多數意見相左。

items.defEn: the breaking up of a body, bond, or moral order
items.usage: 可指議會解散，亦可指道德秩序崩壞。
items.exampleEn: Financial scandal hastened the dissolution of the coalition government.
items.exampleZh: 金融醜聞加速了聯合政府的瓦解。

items.defEn: lack of harmony; a clash of sounds or ideas
items.usage: 音樂用語延伸至認知：cognitive dissonance。
items.exampleEn: There is a striking dissonance between the slogan and the hiring data.
items.exampleZh: 口號與聘用數據之間存在明顯衝突。

items.defEn: swell or stretch from internal pressure
items.usage: 醫學與科學文本常見；過去分詞 distended。
items.exampleEn: The damaged pipe began to distend under rising steam pressure.
items.exampleZh: 受損管線在蒸氣壓力上升下開始膨脹。

items.defEn: extract the essential meaning or most important part
items.usage: GRE 多考比喻義「提煉要點」，不只是蒸餾液體。
items.exampleEn: The brief distills a thousand-page report into five policy options.
items.exampleZh: 這份摘要把千頁報告提煉成五項政策選項。

items.defEn: move or develop in different directions
items.usage: 常見 paths diverge / opinions diverge；反義 converge。
items.exampleEn: After the reform, regional test scores began to diverge sharply.
items.exampleZh: 改革之後，各地測驗分數開始明顯分歧。

items.defEn: strip of possessions, rights, or an association
items.usage: 商管常見 divest assets；亦可指除去權力或身份。
items.exampleEn: The university voted to divest holdings in the disputed industry.
items.exampleZh: 大學表決撤出爭議產業的持股。

items.defEn: make known something private or secret
items.usage: 受詞多為 secrets, names, details；正式語。
items.exampleEn: The clerk refused to divulge patient records without a warrant.
items.exampleZh: 書記員拒絕在無令狀的情況下透露病患紀錄。

items.defEn: a principle or set of beliefs taught as authoritative
items.usage: 法律、宗教、軍事皆常用，如 Monroe Doctrine。
items.exampleEn: The court’s latest ruling refined the doctrine of implied consent.
items.exampleZh: 法院最新判決細化了默示同意之法理。

items.defEn: asserting opinions as if they were unquestionable facts
items.usage: 負面色彩濃，指責人不接受反證。
items.exampleEn: A dogmatic insistence on one model ignored contradictory field data.
items.exampleZh: 對單一模型的武斷堅持忽略了相互矛盾的田野數據。

items.defEn: inactive but capable of becoming active
items.usage: 可指火山、種子、帳戶或潛在衝突。
items.exampleEn: The virus remained dormant in the population for several winters.
items.exampleZh: 該病毒在人群中潛伏了數個冬天。

items.defEn: stern, gloomy, and unfriendly
items.usage: 多形容神情、性格或氣氛，帶蘇格蘭語源色彩。
items.exampleEn: The dour chair cut short any attempt at levity during the hearing.
items.exampleZh: 陰鬱的主席在聽證會上打斷任何輕鬆的嘗試。

items.defEn: doubtful; of questionable quality or honesty
items.usage: 可指人懷疑，亦可指事物本身不可靠。
items.exampleEn: The paper relies on a dubious sample that excludes rural clinics.
items.exampleZh: 該論文倚賴排除鄉村診所的可疑樣本。

items.defEn: deceive; trick someone into believing a falsehood
items.usage: 亦可作名詞，指「受騙者」；GRE 兩義皆考。
items.exampleEn: Phishing emails duped staff into sharing login credentials.
items.exampleZh: 釣魚郵件騙得員工分享登入憑證。

items.defEn: deliberate deceptiveness; double-dealing
items.usage: 強調表裡不一，比 mere lying 更重「雙重面目」。
items.exampleEn: Emails revealed the consultant’s duplicity in advising both sides.
items.exampleZh: 電子郵件揭露顧問同時為雙方出謀的兩面手法。

items.defEn: overflowing with lively enthusiasm
items.defZh: 熱情洋溢的；興高采烈的
items.usage: 正式褒義；語源與「沸騰」相關。
items.exampleEn: The ebullient keynote contrasted with the panel’s cautious forecasts.
items.exampleZh: 熱情洋溢的主題演講與小組謹慎的預測形成對比。

items.defEn: drawing from a variety of sources or styles
items.defZh: 兼收並蓄的；博採眾長的
items.usage: 藝術、學術方法論常用；中性偏褒。
items.exampleEn: Her syllabus is eclectic, mixing primary sources with oral histories.
items.exampleZh: 她的課綱兼收並蓄，將原始文獻與口述史並陳。

items.defEn: an official order or proclamation
items.usage: 帶權威色彩，暗示由上而下發布。
items.exampleEn: The mayor’s edict banned overnight parking along the waterfront.
items.exampleZh: 市長公告禁止濱水區通宵停車。

items.defEn: instruct so as to improve morally or intellectually
items.usage: 語氣正式，常帶道德或智識提升之意。
items.exampleEn: The exhibition aims to edify visitors, not merely entertain them.
items.exampleZh: 展覽旨在啟迪參觀者，而不只是娛樂。

items.defEn: wipe out; make inconspicuous
items.usage: self-effacing 指謙遜低調，GRE 亦常考。
items.exampleEn: Weather and neglect slowly effaced the inscriptions on the monument.
items.exampleZh: 風化與荒廢逐漸抹去紀念碑上的銘文。

items.defEn: bubbly; lively and high-spirited
items.usage: 可指飲料起泡，亦可比喻個性開朗。
items.exampleEn: An effervescent host kept the otherwise technical panel from going dry.
items.exampleZh: 一位活潑的主持人使原本偏技術的討論不至於沉悶。

items.defEn: producing the intended result; effective
items.usage: 正式語，醫學與政策評估常見；強調「真能奏效」。
items.exampleEn: The trial showed the new protocol to be more efficacious than bed rest alone.
items.exampleZh: 試驗顯示新規程比單純臥床休息更有效。

items.defEn: the power to produce a desired effect
items.usage: 學術高頻：vaccine efficacy / policy efficacy。
items.exampleEn: Researchers questioned the efficacy of brief online interventions.
items.exampleZh: 研究人員質疑短暫線上介入的功效。

items.defEn: shameless boldness; insolence
items.usage: 帶強烈譴責；the effrontery to + V 為常見句型。
items.exampleEn: He had the effrontery to demand a bonus after missing every deadline.
items.exampleZh: 他在每個期限都錯過之後，仍厚顏要求獎金。

items.defEn: outstandingly bad; conspicuously wrong
items.defZh: 極其惡劣的；彰顯的錯誤
items.usage: 現代英語幾乎只用於負面；egregious error 為搭配。
items.exampleEn: The audit uncovered egregious conflicts of interest on the board.
items.exampleZh: 稽核揭發董事會極其惡劣的利益衝突。

items.defEn: a poem or speech of lament, usually for the dead
items.usage: 文學體裁；勿與 eulogy（頌詞）完全等同，elegy 更重哀悼。
items.exampleEn: The closing chapter reads as an elegy for a vanishing coastal trade.
items.exampleZh: 終章讀來像是對消逝沿海貿易的輓詩。

items.defEn: draw out a response, fact, or reaction
items.usage: GRE 勿與 illicit（非法的）混淆。
items.exampleEn: Carefully worded questions elicited details the survey had missed.
items.exampleZh: 措辭謹慎的問題引出調查遺漏的細節。

items.defEn: fluent, forceful, and persuasive in expression
items.usage: 可指言辭，亦可指無聲卻有力的表達：eloquent silence。
items.exampleEn: Her eloquent dissent shaped later commentary on the statute.
items.exampleZh: 她雄辯的異議意見形塑了日後對該法條的評註。

items.defEn: make clear; explain in a clarifying way
items.usage: 學術動詞，受詞多為 theory, mechanism, distinction。
items.exampleEn: A simple diagram did more to elucidate the process than ten slides of text.
items.exampleZh: 一張簡圖比十頁文字更能闡明該流程。

items.defEn: escape from; fail to be grasped or achieved
items.defZh: 躲避；使無法理解或達成
items.usage: 可指人逃脫追捕，亦可指意義、成功令人捉摸不定。
items.exampleEn: A precise definition of the term continues to elude the committee.
items.exampleZh: 該詞的精確定義仍令委員會難以掌握。

items.defEn: abnormally thin from starvation or illness
items.defZh: 憔悴消瘦的；骨瘦如柴的
items.usage: 醫學與人道報導用語，程度遠重於 thin。
items.exampleEn: Aid workers found emaciated livestock after the failed harvest.
items.exampleZh: 歉收之後，救援人員發現骨瘦如柴的牲畜。

items.defEn: decorate; add invented details to a story
items.usage: 敘事語境常暗示誇大或虛構細節。
items.exampleEn: Witnesses tend to embellish timelines when memory grows uncertain.
items.exampleZh: 記憶變得不確定時，證人往往會把時間線添枝加葉。

items.defEn: steal money entrusted to one’s care
items.usage: 法律用語；強調資金本是受託保管。
items.exampleEn: The treasurer embezzled grant funds meant for fieldwork.
items.exampleZh: 出納挪用了本應用於田野工作的補助款。

items.defEn: give concrete form to an idea; represent in a tangible way
items.usage: 學術寫作常用 embody the principle / values。
items.exampleEn: The new code is meant to embody the lab’s commitment to open data.
items.exampleZh: 新守則旨在體現實驗室對開放資料的承諾。

items.defEn: in an early, undeveloped stage
items.usage: 比喻義極常見：embryonic industry / plan。
items.exampleEn: Regulation lagged because the sector was still embryonic.
items.exampleZh: 由於該產業仍在萌芽階段，法規相對滯後。

items.defEn: based on observation or experiment rather than theory alone
items.usage: 研究寫作核心詞：empirical evidence / empirical study。
items.exampleEn: The claim lacks empirical support beyond a single case study.
items.exampleZh: 該主張除單一案例外缺乏實證支持。

items.defEn: strive to equal or surpass, especially by imitation
items.usage: 多帶敬意，比 imitate 更有「以之為典範」之意。
items.exampleEn: Young labs often emulate the publishing standards of established groups.
items.exampleZh: 年輕實驗室常效法成熟團隊的發表標準。

items.defEn: a formal expression of high praise
items.usage: 極正式；學術書評或典禮致詞可見。
items.exampleEn: The preface is less a critical essay than an encomium to the mentor.
items.exampleZh: 序言與其說是批評文章，不如說是對導師的頌詞。

items.defEn: native to or regularly found in a particular place
items.usage: GRE 勿與 epidemic（流行、爆發）混淆。
items.exampleEn: Malaria remains endemic in several lowland districts.
items.exampleZh: 瘧疾在若干低地行政區仍屬地方性疾病。

items.defEn: give public approval or support
items.usage: 政治、廣告與學術推薦信皆常用。
items.exampleEn: Three former chairs endorsed the revised ethics statement.
items.exampleZh: 三位前任主席公開支持修訂後的倫理聲明。

items.defEn: drain of energy or vitality
items.usage: GRE 經典陷阱：看起來像 energize，實為「削弱」。
items.exampleEn: Humidity and long hearings combined to enervate the jury.
items.exampleZh: 濕熱與冗長審訊共同使陪審團疲憊不堪。

items.defEn: give rise to; bring into being
items.usage: 正式動詞，受詞多為抽象結果：trust, fear, debate。
items.exampleEn: Opaque pricing can engender suspicion even when costs are fair.
items.exampleZh: 定價不透明即使成本合理，仍可能引發疑慮。

items.defEn: increase in quality, value, or attractiveness
items.usage: 中性偏褒；常見 enhance performance / credibility。
items.exampleEn: Clearer visuals enhanced the report without changing its findings.
items.exampleZh: 更清晰的視覺呈現提升了報告，卻未改變其發現。

items.defEn: a puzzling person or thing; a riddle
items.usage: 形容詞 enigmatic；可指人、文本或現象。
items.exampleEn: The missing dataset remains an enigma to the replication team.
items.exampleZh: 缺失的資料集對複現團隊仍是一個謎。

items.defEn: deep-seated hatred or hostility
items.usage: 程度深於 dislike，常指長期對立。
items.exampleEn: Old border disputes fed lasting enmity between the two ministries.
items.exampleZh: 舊有的邊界爭議助長了兩部會間持久的敵意。

items.defEn: a weary sense of boredom and dissatisfaction
items.usage: 來自法語，帶文學與菁英語感。
items.exampleEn: After the merger, a quiet ennui settled over the research floor.
items.exampleZh: 合併之後，研究樓層瀰漫著一種沉悶的倦怠。

items.defEn: list one by one; count
items.usage: 學術與法律文本常見 enumerate the reasons / rights。
items.exampleEn: The contract enumerates each party’s disclosure duties.
items.exampleZh: 合約逐一列舉各方的揭露義務。

items.defEn: lasting for a very short time
items.usage: 可指時尚、聲名、生命或網路熱點。
items.exampleEn: Online outrage is often ephemeral, but the policy harm can last.
items.exampleZh: 網路憤怒往往短暫，但政策傷害可能持久。

items.defEn: a person with refined taste, especially in food and drink
items.usage: 偏褒，強調品味而非單純貪吃。
items.exampleEn: The critic wrote less as a moralist than as an unapologetic epicure.
items.exampleZh: 那位評論家與其說是道德家，不如說是毫不掩飾的美食家。

items.defEn: a short, witty, and often pointed remark
items.usage: 文學用語；強調簡短而一針見血。
items.exampleEn: The preface ends with an epigram that undercuts the book’s optimism.
items.exampleZh: 序言以一句拆穿全書樂觀語氣的警句作結。

items.defEn: a perfect or typical example of a quality or type
items.usage: the epitome of 為固定搭配。
items.exampleEn: The campus library is the epitome of the university’s open-access ideal.
items.exampleZh: 校園圖書館是該大學開放取用理想的縮影。

items.defEn: mental calmness, especially under strain
items.usage: 正式語，讚賞面對壓力仍能保持平衡。
items.exampleEn: She answered hostile questions with remarkable equanimity.
items.exampleZh: 她以非凡的沉著回應敵對提問。

items.defEn: fair and impartial; just in distributing benefits or burdens
items.usage: 政策與法律高頻：equitable distribution / relief。
items.exampleEn: The board sought an equitable split of patent royalties among labs.
items.exampleZh: 董事會尋求各實驗室之間公平分配專利權利金。

items.defEn: open to more than one interpretation; deliberately ambiguous
items.usage: GRE 常暗示「有意含糊」；unequivocal 為其反義。
items.exampleEn: The minister’s equivocal reply left the funding question unresolved.
items.exampleZh: 部長模稜兩可的答覆使經費問題懸而未決。

items.defEn: use ambiguous language to conceal the truth or avoid commitment
items.usage: 負面動詞，指責人不肯給明確答案。
items.exampleEn: When pressed on timelines, the contractor began to equivocate.
items.exampleZh: 被追問時程時，承包商開始含糊其辭。

items.defEn: destroy completely; wipe out
items.usage: 公共衛生與政策常見 eradicate a disease / poverty。
items.exampleEn: The campaign did not fully eradicate the invasive beetle, but it slowed the spread.
items.exampleZh: 該行動並未徹底根除入侵甲蟲，但減緩了擴散。

items.defEn: irregular and unpredictable in movement or behavior
items.usage: 可修飾人、數據、天氣或機器表現。
items.exampleEn: Erratic funding made it impossible to retain trained technicians.
items.exampleZh: 不穩定的經費使訓練有素的技術人員難以留任。

items.defEn: having or showing deep, scholarly knowledge
items.usage: 正式褒義，常修飾 scholar, commentary, audience。
items.exampleEn: The footnotes reveal an erudite command of both legal and literary sources.
items.exampleZh: 註腳顯示作者對法律與文學文獻皆有淵博掌握。

items.defEn: deliberately avoid or abstain from
items.usage: 正式動詞，帶「主動選擇不用／不碰」之意。
items.exampleEn: The lab eschews proprietary software for all public datasets.
items.exampleZh: 該實驗室對所有公開資料集都避免使用專有軟體。

items.defEn: intended for or understood by a small, initiated group
items.defZh: 艱深的；僅少數人能懂的
items.usage: 可中性指專業門檻高，亦可暗示故作玄奧。
items.exampleEn: The debate grew esoteric once the speakers turned to notation systems.
items.exampleZh: 一旦講者轉入記譜系統，辯論便變得艱深。

items.defEn: worthy of great respect
items.usage: GRE 考「可敬」，不是「可估計的」（那是 estimable 的另一義，較少考）。
items.exampleEn: Even critics called her an estimable public servant with a clean record.
items.exampleZh: 即使批評者也稱她為紀錄清白、值得尊敬的公職人員。

items.defEn: cause to become unfriendly or alienated
items.usage: 常見 be estranged from；名詞 estrangement。
items.exampleEn: A sudden change in authorship rules estranged several longtime collaborators.
items.exampleZh: 作者規則驟變，使數位長期合作者疏遠。

items.defEn: a speech or writing in praise of someone, especially the dead
items.usage: 葬禮語境最常見，亦可比喻過度溢美的評論。
items.exampleEn: The dean’s eulogy emphasized service rather than a list of prizes.
items.exampleZh: 院長的悼詞強調奉獻，而非獎項清單。

items.defEn: a mild or indirect word substituted for one considered harsh
items.usage: 寫作課常提醒：委婉語可能掩蓋責任。
items.exampleEn: “Workforce adjustment” is a euphemism for mass layoffs.
items.exampleZh: 「人力調整」是大規模裁員的委婉說法。

items.defEn: an intense feeling of happiness or well-being
items.usage: 可指真實喜悅，亦可暗示不理性的樂觀。
items.exampleEn: Early trial results produced a euphoria that later data failed to justify.
items.exampleZh: 初期試驗結果帶來後來數據無法支撐的亢奮。

items.defEn: escape or avoid, especially by cleverness or deceit
items.usage: 常見 evade taxes / questions / responsibility，多帶負面。
items.exampleEn: The spokesperson evaded every question about the missing files.
items.exampleZh: 發言人迴避了所有關於缺失檔案的問題。

items.defEn: quickly fading from sight, memory, or existence
items.defZh: 轉瞬即逝的；逐漸消散的
items.usage: 文學色彩濃，比 ephemeral 更強調「正在消逝」。
items.exampleEn: The researcher tried to photograph an evanescent shimmer on the lake.
items.exampleZh: 研究者試圖拍下湖面轉瞬即逝的微光。

items.defEn: make a problem or feeling more severe
items.usage: GRE 勿與 exasperate（使惱怒）混淆。
items.exampleEn: Budget delays exacerbated shortages already caused by the storm.
items.exampleZh: 預算延遲加劇了風暴本已造成的短缺。

items.defEn: making severe demands; requiring great care and precision
items.usage: 可形容人或標準：an exacting editor / exacting standards。
items.exampleEn: The journal’s exacting reviewers rejected papers with sloppy controls.
items.exampleZh: 該期刊嚴苛的審稿人拒絕了控制組草率的論文。

items.defEn: raise in rank, power, or praise
items.usage: 正式語，常見 exalt virtue / a leader。
items.exampleEn: The biography exalts the inventor while barely mentioning the lab team.
items.exampleZh: 這本傳記頌揚發明家，卻幾乎不提實驗室團隊。

items.defEn: irritate intensely
items.usage: 強調反覆刺激後的不耐；形容詞 exasperated / exasperating。
items.exampleEn: Inconsistent citations exasperated the copyeditors more than the typos did.
items.exampleZh: 不一致的引用比錯字更令文字編輯惱怒。

items.defEn: a short passage taken from a longer work
items.usage: 出版與教學常用；亦可作動詞「摘錄」。
items.exampleEn: The syllabus assigns an excerpt from the 1912 field diary, not the whole volume.
items.exampleZh: 課綱指定的是1912年田野日記的摘錄，而非全書。

items.defEn: clear from blame or guilt
items.usage: 法律正式語，與 exonerate 近義。
items.exampleEn: New lab logs helped exculpate the intern accused of deleting the files.
items.exampleZh: 新的實驗紀錄有助為被控刪檔的實習生開脫。

items.defEn: extremely bad or unpleasant
items.usage: 語氣極重的貶義，用於品質或行為。
items.exampleEn: The translation was execrable, turning technical terms into nonsense.
items.exampleZh: 譯文惡劣至極，把術語譯成了胡話。

items.defEn: serving as a desirable model; commendable
items.usage: 多為褒義；法律上 exemplary damages 則指懲罰性賠償。
items.exampleEn: Her documentation was exemplary and became the department template.
items.exampleZh: 她的紀錄堪稱典範，後來成為系上範本。

items.defEn: thorough and complete; leaving nothing out
items.usage: GRE 勿解成「令人精疲力竭的」（那是 exhausting）。
items.exampleEn: An exhaustive search of the archive still yielded no original charter.
items.exampleZh: 對檔案的徹底搜尋仍未找到原始特許狀。

items.defEn: urge strongly; give earnest advice
items.usage: 正式語，帶道德或公共號召色彩。
items.exampleEn: Public-health officials exhorted clinics to report every suspected case.
items.exampleZh: 公衛官員力勸診所通報每一例疑似病例。

items.defEn: an urgent need or pressing situation
items.usage: 正式名詞，複數 exigencies 常見於政策文本。
items.exampleEn: The exigency of the flood overrode ordinary procurement rules.
items.exampleZh: 洪水的緊急狀況凌駕了尋常採購規定。

items.defEn: free from blame or an accusation
items.usage: 法律與職場調查高頻；常接 of 表示被免除的指控。
items.exampleEn: The panel exonerated the chemist of fabricating the chromatograms.
items.exampleZh: 小組洗清了化學家偽造層析圖的嫌疑。

items.defEn: convenient and practical, though possibly improper or unprincipled
items.defZh: 權宜的；方便但不一定正當的
items.usage: GRE 常帶貶義，暗示為求方便而犧牲原則。
items.exampleEn: Releasing a partial dataset was expedient, but it misled later teams.
items.exampleZh: 發布部分資料集是權宜之計，卻誤導了後續團隊。

items.defEn: speed up the progress of
items.usage: 行政與商務常見 expedite a request / shipment。
items.exampleEn: A dedicated liaison helped expedite visa paperwork for visiting scholars.
items.exampleZh: 專責聯絡人協助加快訪問學者的簽證文件。

items.defEn: stated clearly and in detail, leaving no room for confusion
items.usage: 反義 implicit（隱含的）同為 GRE 高頻對。
items.exampleEn: The protocol makes explicit that raw data must be archived within 48 hours.
items.exampleZh: 規程明確規定原始資料須在48小時內歸檔。

items.defEn: use selfishly or unfairly for one’s own advantage
items.usage: GRE 多考負面「佔便宜」；中性「開發資源」較少成為陷阱。
items.exampleEn: The platform exploited unpaid moderators to police toxic content.
items.exampleZh: 該平台利用無薪版主去管制有害內容。

items.defEn: explain in detail
items.usage: 正式學術動詞，常見 expound a theory / on a topic。
items.exampleEn: In the seminar she expounded the distinction between correlation and causation.
items.exampleZh: 研討課上她詳述相關與因果的區別。

items.defEn: still in existence; not destroyed or lost
items.usage: GRE 經典反義聯想：extant ↔ extinct / lost。
items.exampleEn: Only three extant copies of the pamphlet are held in public libraries.
items.exampleZh: 該小冊子僅有三份現存副本收藏於公共圖書館。

items.defEn: spoken or done without preparation
items.usage: 演講與教學語境常見；近義 impromptu。
items.exampleEn: His extemporaneous reply was clearer than the prepared statement.
items.exampleZh: 他的即席回答比預先準備的聲明更清楚。

items.defEn: praise enthusiastically
items.usage: 正式褒義動詞；常見 extol the virtues of。
items.exampleEn: Donors extol the clinic’s outreach, yet they underfund its labs.
items.exampleZh: 捐助者極力讚揚診所的外展，卻對其實驗室資助不足。

items.defEn: irrelevant or unrelated to the subject at hand
items.usage: 寫作與實驗設計常用 extraneous variables / details。
items.exampleEn: The editor cut extraneous anecdotes that slowed the argument.
items.exampleZh: 編輯刪去拖慢論證的無關軼事。

items.defEn: estimate or infer by extending known information
items.usage: 統計與論證高頻；警告樣本不足時不可任意外推。
items.exampleEn: It is risky to extrapolate national trends from one metropolitan sample.
items.exampleZh: 僅憑單一都會樣本去推斷全國趨勢，風險很高。

items.defEn: free from a constraint, snare, or difficulty
items.usage: 常見 extricate oneself from a situation / contract。
items.exampleEn: Legal counsel helped the museum extricate itself from the disputed loan.
items.exampleZh: 法律顧問協助博物館擺脫有爭議的出借協議。

items.defEn: filled with unrestrained energy and liveliness
items.defZh: 精力旺盛的；興高采烈的
items.usage: 可形容人、風格或生長；帶充沛滿溢之感。
items.exampleEn: Exuberant applause followed a paper that few in the room had understood.
items.exampleZh: 熱鬧的掌聲送給了一篇會場裡少有人真正理解的論文。

items.defEn: invent a false story; manufacture
items.usage: GRE 常考「虛構謊言／數據」，不一定是中性的製造。
items.exampleEn: The student fabricated interview quotes that no participant had said.
items.exampleZh: 該學生捏造了沒有任何受訪者說過的引文。

items.defEn: treating serious issues with inappropriate humor
items.defZh: 輕浮開玩笑的；不當幽默的
items.usage: GRE 多帶負面：場合嚴肅卻插科打諢。
items.exampleEn: A facetious remark about layoffs silenced the rest of the meeting.
items.exampleZh: 一句拿裁員開玩笑的輕浮話使會議其餘時間陷入沉默。

items.defEn: make an action or process easier
items.usage: 中性行政動詞；facilitate discussion / access 為搭配。
items.exampleEn: Shared templates facilitate replication across the three field sites.
items.exampleZh: 共用範本使三個田野據點的複現更容易。

items.defEn: a dissenting subgroup within a larger body
items.usage: 政治與組織行為常用；形容詞 factious。
items.exampleEn: A faction within the board blocked the open-data motion.
items.exampleZh: 董事會內一個派系擋下了開放資料動議。

items.defEn: based on a mistaken belief; logically unsound
items.usage: 論證課高頻：fallacious reasoning / a fallacious analogy。
items.exampleEn: It is fallacious to treat correlation in one city as national causation.
items.exampleZh: 把單一城市的相關當成全國因果，是一種謬誤。

items.defEn: left unplanted; inactive
items.usage: 農業本義延伸為「暫時不用的才能／計畫」。
items.exampleEn: After the grant ended, the project lay fallow for two fiscal years.
items.exampleZh: 補助結束後，該計畫閒置了兩個會計年度。

items.defEn: filled with excessive, uncritical zeal
items.usage: 負面多於正面，暗示失去分寸。
items.exampleEn: Fanatical loyalty to one method blinded the team to better tools.
items.exampleZh: 對單一方法的狂熱忠誠，使團隊看不見更好的工具。

items.defEn: very attentive to accuracy and detail; hard to please
items.usage: 可褒（嚴謹）可貶（過分講究）。
items.exampleEn: A fastidious copyeditor caught inconsistencies the authors had missed.
items.exampleZh: 一位一絲不苟的文字編輯抓到作者遺漏的不一致。

items.defEn: understand after much thought; measure the depth of
items.usage: GRE 多考比喻義 cannot fathom why / how。
items.exampleEn: Colleagues could not fathom why the dataset had been deleted overnight.
items.exampleZh: 同事無法理解資料集為何會在一夜之間被刪除。

items.defEn: silly and pointless; smugly foolish
items.usage: 語氣尖銳，指責言論愚蠢卻自信。
items.exampleEn: The press conference ended with a fatuous claim that no one had been harmed.
items.exampleZh: 記者會以「無人受害」的愚昧說法收場。

items.defEn: seek favor by servile flattery
items.usage: GRE 考動詞「諂媚」，不是小鹿名詞；常見 fawn over。
items.exampleEn: Aides who fawn over every joke rarely offer useful criticism.
items.exampleZh: 對每個笑話都巴結附和的助手，很少能提出有用批評。

items.defEn: possible and practical to do
items.usage: 計畫評估高頻：technically feasible / financially feasible。
items.exampleEn: The timeline is ambitious, but a smaller pilot is clearly feasible.
items.exampleZh: 時程野心很大，但較小的試辦計畫顯然可行。
